follow-up time: Until at least 24 hours before delivery
exposure: Women with recurrent pregnancy loss and sole protein S deficiency
Presence or absence of live birth after initial aspirin treatment
cohort: 68 women with recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) and protein S deficiency, which was later narrowed down to 51 women with RPL and sole protein S deficiency after exclusions.
finding: This study suggests that anti-coagulation therapy with low molecular weight heparin is beneficial for women with recurrent pregnancy loss and documented sole protein S deficiency, resulting in a high live birth rate of 94%.
mod_finding: Of the live births in the study, nineteen were delivered vaginally and twenty-eight were delivered by cesarean section.
